summary: An earnings recap whose 'screaming buy' is DLocal (DLO, BUY): he walks through a record quarter — $17.69B TPV, record revenue and gross profit dollars, net income up 28% — arguing the market misunderstands the model, which optimizes for absolute gross-profit dollars, not take rate; excluding one large merchant's volume-tier ramp, take rate was flat while TPV grew 65%+. With TPV guidance raised to 60-70% growth, PEG of 0.8, and a $4B market cap, he is accumulating and sees a multi-bagger or take-private outcome. He also bought more Meta (BUY) under $600, calling it disrespected and extremely attractive, and previews Micron's September report expecting excellent growth with supply nowhere near demand. Nu Holdings gets a detailed review: first $1B+ net-income quarter (+49% YoY), record 33% ROE and 12.4% risk-adjusted NIM (partly one-off from Brazil's Desenrola program), 139M customers, Mexico breaking even in six years, and a measured US entry — cheap and, in his view, a future $100B+ company. He defends the AI capex cycle broadly: when spending eventually slows, core profitability will surface and today's extreme price-to-FCF multiples will normalize, and he pushes back on analysts who endlessly ask 'what about 2028?' for AI names but never for banks or consumer stocks. IREN gets a mention: hated neo-cloud name reporting August 27 that could pop like CoreWeave/Nebius if it shows progress toward its ARR target.
